title: Public-coin communication complexity of equality
statement:
For every natural number $n$ and every real $\varepsilon > 0$, the $\varepsilon$-error public-coin randomized communication complexity of the equality function $\mathrm{equality}_n$ on pairs of $n$-bit Boolean strings satisfies
\[
  \mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_\varepsilon(\mathrm{equality}_n)
  \;\le\;
  \left\lceil \log_2\!\left(\lceil \varepsilon^{-1}\rceil + 1\right)\right\rceil + 1,
\]
where $\lceil \varepsilon^{-1}\rceil$ denotes the least natural number at least $\varepsilon^{-1}$ and $\lceil\,\cdot\,\rceil$ inside the logarithm the ceiling of the base-$2$ logarithm. That is, there is a public-coin protocol computing $\mathrm{equality}_n$ with error probability at most $\varepsilon$ on every input pair whose worst-case number of exchanged bits is bounded by this quantity.
hypotheses_covered: ε is a positive real (0 < ε)
